newsitem.title: USA: Eurobond success opens Russia to more scrutiny.
newsitem.headline: Eurobond success opens Russia to more scrutiny.

text.p: Russia's grand entrance in the Eurobond market has brought a better understanding of the macroeconomic forces shaping the country to global investors, who will demand to be informed of the progress, U.S. market sources said.
Under the spotlight that zoomed in on them in roadshows from Asia to Europe to the U.S., senior Russian officials made their case to inquisitive investors.
"Until then the macroeconomic stabilization plan had not been well explained," said Kurt Schmidt, executive vice preisdent at SBC/Warburg. "The information distributed on Russia was well received."
The image of modern-day Russia improved as investors came to view it as more than just the wild and unaccountable rubble of a collapsed empire, he said.

Russia raised $1 billion through five-year notes with a 9-1/4 percent coupon to yield 345 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries. Now, the nation's new creditors will insist on more reliable and transparent economic data.
"The proceeds will go into a general pot, perhaps to pay off some arrears," said a manager. "We have to watch the fiscal deficits."

Lawrence Brainard, head of emerging markets research at Chase Securities, warned that the the $1 billion proceeds from the Eurobond would not make it less urgent for Russia to receive a delayed tranche of a $10 billion loan from the International Monetary Fund.
"The tax revenues shortfall is a long-term problem," Brainard said, predicting the IMF would want to see a trend -- perhaps over three months -- before disburing the funds.
The IMF problems mean at least $650 million of credits budgeted for this year may not be paid until 1997.

Because the Eurobond is issued in the U.S. under the 144A rule of the Securities and Exchange Commission and sold to qualified institutional buyers, J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg -- the joint lead managers -- declined comment on the allocation or details of the placement.
Traders noted that the pricing of the maiden eurobond gave an expected lift to Russian Minfins, but turnover was slow.
Earlier on Thursday, Moscow police also released $56.81 million of the Minfin bonds which had been frozen since June.
"Minfins were well bid, but most of the good news is already in the market," said a trader.
Minfin 3 rose 3/4 to bid 83-3/4, and Minfin 4 gained 5/8 to bid 60-7/8.
But another trader said the Minfins could appreciate after the Eurobond begins trading on the secondary market.

Compared to the Eurobond, which has a duration of 4.2 years and a yield of 345 basis points over U.S. Treasury, Minfin 3 has half of the duration and trades 163 basis points over the Eurobond. Minfin 4 has a duration of five years and traders 230 bp over the Eurobond, he said.
"There is a lot of room for the spread (over Eurobond) to narrow," the trader said.
